summary: Johann Tobias Beck was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1822–1826). He later held posts at the University of Basel (~1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843–1878).

Working in Indology and other fields, Pfaff studied at Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen. He held posts at Tübinger Stift, Melanchthon-Gymnasium, and as mathematics professor at the universities of Tartu (1803), Würzburg (1817), and Erlangen-Nürnberg (1818).

A scholar of Indology and archaeology, she studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She taught Sanskrit at Groningen, lectured at Cambridge, and served as Director of the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at Amsterdam (1958–1983).

Johanna Narten was an Indology, Iranian, and linguistics scholar. She studied under Ernst Zinn at Saarland University and earned her PhD at Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann, where she was later an assistant (1973–1977).

Johannes Beltz is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies in 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche.

Johannes Bronkhorst works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at VU Amsterdam, Rajasthan, Savitribai Phule Pune under S. D. Joshi, and Leiden. He served at Leiden and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (1987–2011).

Indologist Johannes Hertel earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig (1892–1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920) before holding the chair for Indian philology at the University of Leipzig (1919–1937).

Indologist Johannes Klatt studied under Albrecht Weber and completed his doctorate at the University of Halle (~1869–1873). From 1872, he worked at the Prussian State Library, serving as custodian from 1880 and librarian from 1889.

Johannes Nobel worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, served at the Prussian State Library and University of Berlin, and held the Indology chair at Marburg (1928–1955).

Scholar of Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies Johannes Rahder earned his doctorate at Utrecht University. He held posts at Utrecht, Leiden (Chair of Japanese, 1931–1946), the University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale University (1947–1965).

Johannes Schmidt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn, Jena under August Schleicher, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1868), University of Graz (1873–1876), and University of Berlin (1876).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Magister at the University of Marburg, he held posts at Free University of Berlin and the University of Munich, becoming außerplanmäßiger Professor of Indology in 2014.

Johannes Schubert specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under multiple scholars. He worked at Leipzig University Library (~1927–1954) and taught Tibetan and Mongolian at the University of Leipzig (1934–1945; 1952–1962).
John A. Ardussi is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology. Supervised by Turrell V. Wylie for his MA, he earned his PhD from Australian National University and became a research team member at CNRS.

John Alexander Jorgensen specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at Australian National University under Kenneth Herbert Joseph Gardiner, later holding posts at ANU and Griffith University.

John Alexander Stewart was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903). After serving in the Indian Civil Service, he held posts at University College London (~1933–1936) and SOAS (~1936–1948).

John Allan worked in Indology and archaeology, studying at Edinburgh and Leipzig. He served at the British Museum from 1907 (Keeper of Coins and Medals, 1931) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst, under William Dwight Whitney, and at Tübingen and Berlin. He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).

John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist educated at Edinburgh. He served Fort William College as principal (1800–1804), taught for the East India Company, and became University College London's first Professor of Hindustani (~1828–1831).
